deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. The page sets up the complex-variable theory of stereographic projection of the unit sphere. It then determines which linear fractional maps between two stereographic representations of the same sphere come from a rigid motion of the sphere. NOTATION: a lower-case letter and the same letter in upper case denote conjugates, so A = conj(a). The sphere radius is 1. n is the linear magnification ratio (Vergrößerungsverhältniß).

(1) At the point with complex coordinate a, n = 1 + aA = 1+|a|^2. [Mine: with equator-plane coordinates the true ratio plane/sphere is (1+|a|^2)/2. So Gauss's n is the scale normalised to 1 at the centre. Equivalently, it is the projection onto the tangent plane at the opposite pole with coordinate a = w/2.]

(2) The antipode of a is -1/A (standard). There n = 1 + 1/(aA) = (1+aA)/(aA).

(3) The 'bicomplex' number a (an ordinary point x+iy of the plane) corresponds to the 'tricomplex' point (2a + (1-aA)η)/(1+aA) on the sphere. Here η is a third unit along the polar axis. This is inverse stereographic projection: (X+iY, Z) = (2a, 1-|a|^2)/(1+|a|^2). a=0 goes to the pole +η, and a=∞ goes to -η. Its norm is 1 because 4|a|^2 + (1-|a|^2)^2 = (1+|a|^2)^2.

(4) General change of representation: t' = (at-b)/(ct+d), where t and t' are the coordinates of the same sphere point in the first and second representation.
- Magnification of the sphere→t'-plane map: n' = |dt'/dt| n = |ad+bc|/|ct+d|^2 (1+tT). The determinant is ad+bc because of the sign -b; Gauss writes ad-bc here, see errors.
- If the new representation is again a stereographic projection of the same sphere (a rotation), then n' must equal 1+|t'|^2. That function has its minimum 1 at t'=0.
- Minimum of n' over t: by Lagrange's identity (cC+dD)(1+tT) - |ct+d|^2 = |c - dT|^2 ≥ 0, so |ct+d|^2/(1+tT) ≤ cC+dD. Equality holds at t = C/D, where ct+d = (cC+dD)/D and 1+tT = (cC+dD)/(dD).
- Hence min n' = Mod (ad+bc)/(cC+dD) · |D/d| = Mod (ad+bc)/(cC+dD).
- Requiring the minimum to sit at t'=0: t'(C/D)=0 gives aC = bD. Then ad+bc = a(dD+cC)/D, so n'_min = Mod a/D = Mod b/C.
- Requiring n'_min = 1 forces |a|=|d| and |b|=|c|. With |ε|=1 one may put d = εA, i.e. εD = a. Then aC = bD gives εC = b, i.e. c = εB. Gauss writes 'εC = b, εD = a', the written 'd'/'a' being corrections.
- Replacing a,b,c,d by √ε·a, √ε·b, √ε·c, √ε·d multiplies all four by a common factor, so t' is unchanged. Since conj(√ε) = 1/√ε, this gives c = B, d = A.
- Final rotation formula: t' = (at-b)/(Bt+A), with inverse t = (At'+b)/(-Bt'+a). [Check, mine: |Bt+A|^2 + |at-b|^2 = (aA+bB)(1+tT), so n' = (aA+bB)(1+tT)/|Bt+A|^2 = 1+t'T' identically. No normalisation aA+bB=1 is needed.]

This is the Cayley–Klein / SU(2) form of the Möbius transformations induced by rotations of the sphere. Gauss derives it by a magnification-minimum argument.
errors: In 'Hier wird n' = Mod (ad-bc)/(ct+d)^2 (1+tT)' the determinant should be ad+bc, since the map is (at-b)/(ct+d). Gauss himself uses ad+bc in the next lines, and his later steps (n'=Mod a/D) are correct only with +.

The intermediate expression of the minimum as transcribed, Mod (ad+bc)/(cC+dD)^2 · D/d, is dimensionally inconsistent with the stated equality. The correct intermediate is (ad+bc)·D^2/(cC+dD)^2 · (cC+dD)/(dD) = (ad+bc)/(cC+dD) · D/d. Either Gauss's squared bracket stood for ((cC+dD)/D)^2 with a factor omitted, or the '^2' is a misreading. The final value Mod (ad+bc)/(cC+dD) is correct.
Minor gap: Gauss does not state why 'minimum 1 at t'=0' suffices for the map to be a rotation. It does suffice, and the resulting form satisfies n' = 1+t'T' identically.

n = 1+aA is the magnification only up to a constant factor 2 for the equatorial-plane convention implied by the antipode -1/A and by formula 3. It must be read as relative magnification (=1 at the centre).

results.what: Linear magnification of stereographic projection n = 1+|a|^2, and value (1+|a|^2)/|a|^2 at the antipode -1/conj(a)
results.modern_name: conformal factor of stereographic projection; antipodal map z -> -1/conj(z)
results.usually_credited_to: classical (Ptolemy/Hipparchus for the projection; Harriot/Halley for conformality; Lambert for scale formulas)

results.what: Inverse stereographic projection written as a 'tricomplex' number (2a+(1-|a|^2)η)/(1+|a|^2)
results.modern_name: inverse stereographic projection to the unit sphere (Riemann sphere coordinates)
results.usually_credited_to: standard; complex formulation usually associated with Riemann/Neumann (1850s-60s)

results.what: Magnification of a Möbius change of chart: n' = |ad+bc|(1+|t|^2)/|ct+d|^2, minimized at t = conj(c)/conj(d) with minimum |ad+bc|/(|c|^2+|d|^2) (via Lagrange/Cauchy–Schwarz)
results.modern_name: spherical derivative / chordal Lipschitz factor of a Möbius transformation
results.usually_credited_to: 19th-century function theory (e.g. Klein school); no single attribution

results.what: Characterisation of rotations of the sphere as linear fractional maps t' = (at-b)/(conj(b) t + conj(a)), with inverse t = (conj(a)t'+b)/(-conj(b)t'+a)
results.modern_name: Cayley–Klein parameters; SU(2) -> SO(3) via Möbius transformations
results.usually_credited_to: Cayley (1879), Klein (1875-1884), with Euler–Rodrigues (1775/1840) for the parameters

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's anticipation of quaternion/Euler–Rodrigues rotation formulas ('Mutationen des Raumes') is well known, and notes on stereographic projection appear in Werke VIII. So the existence of such material is not shocking. Still, an explicit derivation of the SU(2)/Cayley–Klein Möbius form of sphere rotations, via a neat magnification-minimum argument, predates Cayley and Klein. It is a notable unpublished-style detail, though it is possibly already printed in the Werke (I am unsure).

transcription_corrections: 'Hier wird n' = Mod (ad-bc)/(ct+d)^2 (1+tT)': the image indeed reads 'ad - bc'. This is Gauss's sign slip (should be ad+bc); the transcription is faithful.

In the minimum formula the denominator transcribed '(cC+dD)^2' is uncertain in the image (a bracket with a superscript-like stroke). It may be '((cC+dD)/D)^2'-type shorthand or a misreading; mathematically '(cC+dD)·d' times D is required.
In the final denominator 'cC+dD' the 'C' is written over another letter (a correction) in the manuscript.
'εC = b, εD = a': in the manuscript 'b' and 'a' are corrections over other letters ('d...' and a struck letter), consistent with the transcription.
'wo t, t'': the manuscript has 't' with an apparent overwrite ('wo t t'' with a struck 'sich'-like word). The reading 'sich auf Einerlei Punkt' is fine.
